I will keep to the crop pattern I know best in Quzhou County: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. I farm this way because it fits our local water, weather, and work rhythm, and it gives me grain from two seasons instead of betting everything on one crop. At the start of the year, my wheat is already in the field from last autumn, so I will manage that crop through spring with topdressing, irrigation at the key stages, and a couple of pesticide sprays if disease, aphids, or weeds show up. After wheat harvest, I will quickly prepare the field and plant summer maize, using seed that is reliable and commonly used here, because I want steady yield and simple field management rather than extra risk. I will use moderate fertilizer, not too little and not too much, because I need the crop to stand well and fill grain, but I also cannot waste money on unnecessary input. I will irrigate only at the most important times, since water matters, and I will keep tillage simple with rotary tillage so I can turn the season quickly between wheat and maize. My whole plan is to stay with familiar crops, control costs, protect yield, and avoid management that is too complicated.
